name: Ivy Knight
life: “I still remember hearing my first record with one ear covered.” Thursday often includes a stop at Paper & Pine Books, where Ivy starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I'm deaf in one ear. The landing is the only place in this building where I hear the bass clearly.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a red windbreaker and a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. Ivy has a long face and high cheekbones, with short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. Ivy presses the lips together to keep a smile in during a conversation.
personality: Ivy treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Ivy lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To reserve a listening spot for the working bass register.
family: Nora Nolasco is Ivy’s second cousin. Ivy saves a place. Nora chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *Station steps in rain*, Nora says, “I brought a petition and the names ran together.”
connections: John Collins. A street recording lets the neighbor compare how the bass sounds outside.

reactions.situation: The owner asks a child to play first
reactions.response: Ivy finds a steady seat for the child and waits for the opening notes.

reactions.situation: An unfamiliar person asks for directions but cannot read the street signs
reactions.response: Ivy draws the route by its turns and entrances and has the person show which turn comes first.

reactions.situation: When offered a favor with ambiguous terms
reactions.response: Ivy says what can be returned and asks whether that will do.
